clue.text: Blame Sean, a bad sailor

indicators.note: something bad is spoiled or broken, so the letters before it are put into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these three words, taken together

explanation.surface: Someone pins the blame on Sean, who has turned out to be a poor sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: An able seaman is a rating in the navy, a sailor of the rank above ordinary seaman.

clue.text: A reptile seizing bait at sea, like a dolphin?

indicators.note: to seize something is to grab hold of it, so one piece wraps around another
being at sea means confused and all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
a croc is short for a crocodile, a reptile
taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: A crocodile snapping up bait thrown into the sea, perhaps leaping like a dolphin.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled bait goes inside CROC, after the opening A. The question mark marks the definition as an example: dolphins leap and twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolphins are famous for leaping and somersaulting, the agile gymnastic movement of an acrobat.

clue.text: Soldier in pub is rational

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it

blocks.note: your local is the pub you regularly drink in
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier who drinks in the pub is being perfectly sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: A local, in British usage, is the pub nearest your home.
explanation.definitionFit: Logical reasoning follows sound principles, which is exactly what a rational person does.

clue.text: One providing reports on sports day?

definitions.text: One providing reports on sports day?

blocks.clueFragment: One providing reports on sports day?
blocks.note: surface reading: a journalist writing up the school sports day for the paper
setter's reading: reports are loud bangs, like the one fired to begin each race

explanation.walkthrough: 'Reports' looks like news coverage, but a report is also the sound of a gun going off.
explanation.definitionFit: The gun fired to begin each race at an athletics meeting makes a sharp bang, called a report.

clue.text: Handy worker, painter, hasn't finished on article

indicators.note: not finishing means stopping short, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a painter is an artist
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A handyman who is also a painter hasn't yet finished work on some article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On article' puts the shortened painter on top of, here before, the article.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual craftsman, someone good with their hands.

clue.text: Description of a nobleman, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the words are judged by their sound

blocks.note: a count is a European nobleman

explanation.surface: Someone gives a description of a nobleman they have heard about.
explanation.definitionFit: An account is a report or narrative of events, a description of what happened.

clue.text: Junk mail — plans for circulation

indicators.note: something put into circulation goes round, so the word is turned back to front

blocks.note: maps are plans, as of a town or building

explanation.surface: Unsolicited mail is just someone's plans sent out for circulation.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is unsolicited bulk email, the electronic equivalent of junk mail.

clue.text: Tramp cut off in enclosed field

blocks.note: to pad is to tramp, walking steadily on foot
to dock a tail is to cut it off

explanation.surface: A tramp is cut off, stranded in a fenced field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' looks like a noun, a vagrant, but here it is the verb to walk heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddock is a small fenced field, typically where horses are kept or exercised.

clue.text: Start to signal in additional code

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept
one thing being in another means it sits inside it

blocks.note: more means additional, extra
the opening letter of signal

explanation.surface: An instruction to begin signalling using an extra code.
explanation.definitionFit: Morse is the telegraph code of dots and dashes devised by Samuel Morse.

clue.text: This should be used when driving off at first

definitions.text: This should be used when driving off at first

blocks.note: surface reading: driving off sounds like playing the opening golf shot, or chasing someone away

blocks.clueFragment: This should be used when driving off at first
blocks.note: setter's reading: before pulling away in a car you check behind you first

explanation.walkthrough: Driving instructors teach mirror, signal, manoeuvre: look behind before moving off from the kerb.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver checks the glass above the windscreen, showing traffic behind, before setting off from a parked position.

clue.text: Fury about National Trust exercising power

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: fury is great anger
NT is the standard abbreviation for the National Trust

explanation.surface: Someone is furious about the National Trust and the way it wields its authority.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is the British charity that looks after historic houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Regnant means reigning, as in a queen regnant, so it describes a ruler actually holding power.

clue.text: Small child has unusual dread of cheese

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so the letters are taken out of order

blocks.note: ch is the short form of child
the letters of dread, rearranged

explanation.surface: A little child has a strange fear of cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' tells you to use the shortened form of child.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheddar is a hard English cheese named after a village in Somerset.

clue.text: Start from scratch and cook — banquets are difficult!

indicators.note: something difficult is awkward and troublesome, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters of these three words, taken together

explanation.surface: A chef complains that banquets are hard work and it is time to begin all over again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like an instruction, an anagram signal, but it is part of the material and 'difficult' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Going back to square one is an idiom for returning to the beginning after a failed attempt.

clue.text: What's used by parrot? A long claw

indicators.note: the letters needed are the ones put to use within the following words, sitting inside them

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of parrot through a into long

explanation.surface: A question about what a parrot uses, answered with a long claw.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark breaks the surface in two, but the hidden letters run straight across it.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is the hooked claw of a bird, especially a bird of prey.

clue.text: Fool, one who chooses to become a pedantic fault-finder

blocks.note: a nit, short for nitwit, is a fool
someone who picks is one who chooses

explanation.surface: A foolish person who decides to turn into a petty critic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' looks like the usual I, but it belongs to the phrase for someone who selects.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitpicker is someone who looks for tiny trivial errors, an overly fussy critic.

clue.text: Colour of your label originally

indicators.note: done originally means done in a novel, inventive way, so the letters are freshly arranged

blocks.note: the letters of these two words, taken together

explanation.surface: Asking what colour your label was at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' usually signals first letters, but here it means in an original fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal blue is a deep vivid shade of blue, named for its association with the British royal family.

clue.text: Flying to a place inhabited by king and queen

indicators.note: things flying are scattered through the air, so these letters are thrown into a new order
a place inhabited by someone has them living inside it

blocks.note: the letters of these three words, rearranged
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king and queen fly off together to a place where they live.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra was the last ruling queen of ancient Egypt, lover of Mark Antony.

clue.text: Boffin using short gadget he developed

indicators.note: something short is missing its end, so the last letter is cut
something developed has been worked up into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: gadget without its final letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scientist uses a small device that he invented himself.
explanation.walkthrough: A boffin is British slang for a scientist or technical expert.
explanation.definitionFit: An egghead is an informal word for an intellectual, which matches the brainy scientist a boffin is.

clue.text: See some of orchestra (in error) getting coach

indicators.note: only some of the following words are used, a run of letters lying inside them

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of orchestra through in into error

explanation.surface: Watch part of the orchestra make a mistake and get extra coaching.
explanation.walkthrough: The brackets are surface dressing; the hidden letters run straight through them.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer coaches athletes or teams, preparing them for competition.

clue.text: A large amount journalist collected

blocks.note: taken as written
a mass is a large amount
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A journalist gathered a large quantity of material.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather a great quantity together, so amassed means collected or accumulated.

clue.text: Despicable person, close to forty, grovelling

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: a worm is a contemptible, weak person
the last letter of forty

explanation.surface: A contemptible person, nearly forty years old, crawling to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to forty' looks like an age, but it means the end letter of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Wormy here means behaving like a worm, abjectly servile and crawling, as a grovelling person does.

clue.text: Our dean translated poem

indicators.note: something translated is turned into a different form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these two words, taken together

explanation.surface: The head of our college has rendered a poem into another language.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondeau is a French verse form of thirteen or so lines on two rhymes with a refrain.

clue.text: Major here in Georgia

blocks.note: surface reading: an army major stationed in Georgia, the country or the US state
setter's reading: a major is one of golf's four chief tournaments, one of which is played at a famous club in Georgia

explanation.walkthrough: The Masters, one of golf's majors, is held every April at this course in the city of Augusta, Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: The golf club that hosts the Masters every year sits in Augusta, Georgia, so a major is played there.

clue.text: Tree has less on top, having been pollarded

indicators.note: a pollarded tree has had its top cut off, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: someone balder has less hair on top of the head

explanation.surface: A tree has fewer branches at its crown after being cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: Pollarding is a real thing done to trees, which hides that it is the deletion signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a tree of the birch family that grows in damp ground beside rivers.

clue.text: Girl and boy have to become calm

blocks.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
Ed is a boy's name, short for Edward
to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: A girl and a boy have to settle down.
explanation.definitionFit: When wind or excitement dies down it subsides and grows quieter, so things become calm.

clue.text: Bizarre, as ruler? Awfully

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so these letters come out in a mess

blocks.note: the letters of these two words, taken together

explanation.surface: Someone finds a person's conduct as ruler terribly strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Surreal means dreamlike and strange, like the art of the Surrealist movement, hence bizarre.

clue.text: Leader of expedition on free trip

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front, the only one kept

blocks.note: to rid is to free, as of a nuisance
the opening letter of expedition

explanation.surface: The head of an expedition goes on a holiday for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' in an across clue lets the first piece come after the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A ride is a journey on horseback or in a vehicle, a short trip.

clue.text: Caravans may follow it, a winding detour during endlessly long hard journey

indicators.note: a winding path twists about, so these letters are twisted into a new order
without an end means the final letter is dropped
something happening during another sits within its span, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written, then mixed with the next word
taken as written, then mixed with the previous word
a trek is a long arduous journey

explanation.surface: A camel caravan follows a twisting detour on a long, gruelling desert journey.
explanation.walkthrough: The caravans are trains of merchants and camels, not holiday trailers.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade route is a path used by merchants, such as the Silk Road along which camel caravans travelled.
